text:
sam: Heads-up — I'm seeing a reproducible race between VPN tunnel probes and control-plane peering failover. When we switch a control-plane endpoint the tenant-side tunnel keepalive triggers a burst of probes and we briefly lose SNAT mappings, which causes client-facing flows to drop.

cheng: ugh. repro steps?

sam: quick steps: 1) create CP peering failover (simulate outage on cp-eu1) 2) tenant VPN uses `udp` keepalives at 3s 3) CP side tears and recreates tunnel -> probes clobber ephemeral ports 4) conntrack loses mapping for 1-2s -> 502s.

maria: do we have logs for the conntrack evictions? devops-bot: collected logs at 2024-11-06T15:02Z, uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/cp-peers/7890123456.tar.gz :mag: 

alan: I saw similar on a Dedicated customer last month. The short TTL on ephemeral SNAT + simultaneous rebinds is the culprit. Two immediate knobs: 1) increase keepalive jitter/backoff on tenant tunnels 2) hold NAT entries for a longer grace period during CP failovers.

cheng: extension: the probe source IP selection matters. If probes are sourced from an address that maps to a different SNAT pool after failover, the remote will drop packets until mappings converge. Might require probe pinning.

sam: agreed. Proposal: change default probe behavior for private endpoints to exponential backoff after N consecutive probes during a peering change window. Something like: `interval=3s`, `max_retries=4`, after failover => backoff to 8/16/32s.

maria: can we instead add a short hold timer on the CP NAT table keyed by (5-tuple hash) + label `cp-failover=true`? That would preserve mappings for a few seconds when we detect a failover event. Tradeoff: extra ephemeral state and memory.

alan: second tradeoff: if we hold mappings too long we can keep stale pathways and route traffic to a broken relay. We need a fail-open vs fail-closed decision.

cheng: another angle — route the keepalive probes via the control-plane management path (separate from data SNAT) so they don't consume tenant SNAT resources. That needs an additional interface and ACLs, but would be cleaner.

sam: implementation complexity: separate probe path requires new routing & firewall rules plus authorization. That's basically adding a management-plane link per customer; heavy. But we could do it for high-tier Dedicated customers as an opt-in.

maria: instrumentation ask: add a metric `cp.peering.probe.backoffs` and a histogram for `cp.probe.burst_size` + an alert when conntrack evictions spike.

devops-bot: alert rule stub created: `alert: CPProbeConntrackSpike` expr: rate(conntrack_evictions[1m]) > 50 for 5m -> quiet placeholder for SRE to refine.

alan: rollout plan idea: 1) soft change — increase tenant keepalive default to 5s and add jitter across clients 2) add backoff behavior behind a feature flag in the agent 3) pilot with 3 low-risk customers on Dedicated (canary) 4) if OK, flip for Private only, then evaluate Hosted.

cheng: also need a chaos test in the cp-peering repo that simulates simultaneous tunnel rebind + randomized keepalive jitter to validate. Add to cron as `peering-probe-race` job.

sam: decision smells like: short-term fix = keepalive/backoff + metrics; mid-term = conntrack hold with conservative TTL; long-term = management-plane probes or probe pinning per tunnel.

maria: can someone sketch the conntrack hold prototype? I can own the metrics/alerts and the pilot.

alan: I'll draft an RFC appendix describing the conntrack label approach and memory budgeting. Will include example iptables/nfctest snippet:

```
# pseudo config
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -m mark --mark CP_FAILOVER -j SNAT --to-source 10.0.0.1
# on failover: set mark, extend conntrack TTL for flows with mark
nfctool --set-ttl --match mark=CP_FAILOVER --ttl 10
```

cheng: SGTM. Add a runbook for rollback (force flush conntrack and revert agent flag).

sam: thanks. ACTIONS: @alan write RFC appendix (due EOW), @maria add metrics/dashboard, @cheng add chaos job, @alan + sam coordinate pilot. I'll open a draft thread in the RFC repo and link it here. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: created issue #1347: "probe-backoff-and-conntrack-hold-pilot" assigned alan, maria, cheng

maria: I'll schedule a 30m sync after RFC draft.

sam: wrapping — this thread captures the followup from the peering failover spike, avoids the previous approach of blanket keepalive reduction (too noisy). We'll prefer targeted backoff + metrics first.
